title: Surface Engineering of Pancreatic Islets with a Heparinized StarPEG Nanocoating
protocol: Weigh out 0.69 g of heparin and dissolve in 2.0 mL of ice-cold deionized water.
Weigh out 0.23 g of NHS and dissolve in 0.5 mL of ice-cold deionized water in a round-bottom flask.
Weigh out 0.77 g of EDC and dissolve in 0.5 mL of ice-cold deionized water in a round-bottom flask.
Mix the NHS and EDC solutions in a round-bottom flask.
Leave the mixed solution on the bench at room temperature for 30 min.
Centrifuge the EDC NHS mixture at 5,031 x g for 10 min to remove excess EDC and NHS.
Add 30 mL of cold ethanol to the mixture solution and centrifuge at 5,031 x g for 10 min.
Repeat the ethanol addition and centrifugation twice more.
Add 1.0 mL of 10% (w/v) starPEG-(NH2)8 to a round-bottom flask.
Add 0.67 mL of 10% (w/v) heparin-NHS to the same round-bottom flask.
Place the mixed solution of starPEG-(NH2)8 and heparin-NHS in an incubator at 25 °C for 20 min to obtain a clear solution with viscosity.
Rinse the agate mortar, pestle, and pelleting device with acetone.
Dry the glassware in an oven before use.
Mix approximately 0.1–1% heparin-PEG sample with 200–250 mg of fine KBr powder.
Place the heparin-PEG and KBr mixture in the agate mortar and finely pulverize into small pellets.
Transfer the mixture into a pelleting device.
Apply high compression force (8 T/cm²) in a vacuum for 1–2 min to form transparent pellets.
Gently pull the sample pellets away from the pelleting device.
Transfer the sample pellets very carefully to a Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscope.
Prepare standard 48-well cell culture plate and pipettes.
Pipette the heparin-PEG copolymer solution into the wells of a 48-well culture plate.
Freeze the plate at -80 °C for 24 h.
Lyophilize the samples at -50 °C in vacuum environment (0.1 Pa) for 24 h.
Spread samples across the sticky surface of an aluminum stub.
Coat the samples with gold.
Observe under the scanned electron microscope to observe internal porous structures.
Examine the heparin-PEG nanocoating surface by atomic force microscopy (AFM).
Clean silica glass slides with piranha solution (70% H2SO4, 30% H2O2) at 80 °C for 40 min.
Sonicate the slides in methanol for 10 min and then in toluene for 10 min.
Dry the slides by vacuum drying.
Wash the slides with plenty of 3-aminopropyl-triethoxysilane solution (2% in toluene), shaking gently.
Sonicate the slides in methanol for 10 min, then in toluene for 10 min.
Place 100 µL of 3% heparin-PEG solution across the surface of the slides using a standard pipette.
Extract mouse islets by collagenase digestion and histopaque gradient purification as previously reported.
Handpick 200 islets under a dissection microscope to a 1.5 mL tube.
Add 500 µL of PBS to the islets and centrifuge at 503 x g for 1 min.
Remove the supernatant and add 250 µL of the heparin-PEG solution, keeping the mixture on ice for 10 min.
Pipette up and down to allow the islets to mix well with the heparin-PEG solution.
Centrifuge at 503 x g for 1 min.
Remove the supernatant and add 500 µL of PBS.
Pipette up and down to mix well.
Centrifuge at 503 x g for 1 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Add 1–2 mL of RPMI 1640 supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum to the coated islets.
Transfer these islets into a non-charged sterile bacterial culture dish.
Observe the morphology and fluorescence signals of FAM-heparin-PEG nanocoating-coated islets under an inverted fluorescence microscope.
Handpick 20 of the heparin-PEG coated mouse islets.
Place 20 heparin-PEG coated mouse islets into each well of a 96-well cell culture plate for a total of 10 wells.
Handpick 20 noncoated control islets.
Place 20 noncoated control islets into one well of the same 96-well cell culture plate for a total of 10 wells each.
Put 200 µL of RPMI 1640 supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum into each well containing islets.
Maintain in culture for 14 days.
Replace islet culture media every 2 days.
Treat the islets with a live/dead staining kit at the end of 14 days in culture.
Observe under an inverted fluorescence microscope.
Count PI+ (red) cells within each islet under an inverted fluorescence microscope.
Pre-cool all experimental plastics including culture plate and pipette tips at least 12 h before use.
Place a 24-well plate on a cooling pad.
Add 250 µL of ice cold growth factor-reduced Matrigel into each well of a 24-well cell culture plate.
Place the coated 24-well plate at 4 °C for at least 30 min.
Remove all culture media from the tissue culture flask.
Rinse the flask with 5 mL of PBS.
Add 3 mL of trypsin-EDTA to the flask.
Incubate at 37 °C for 3 min in a standard incubator.
Lightly tap the bottom of the flask to detach the cells.
Add 5 mL of serum-supplemented media into the flask.
Collect detached cells into a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 1,000 x g for 5 min.
Take off the supernatant and add 5 mL of PBS to the cell pellet.
Pipette up and down to mix well.
Centrifuge at 1,000 x g for 5 min again.
Add serum-supplemented DMEM media into the tube with cells.
Seed 50,000 MS1 cells into each well of the matrix-solution-coated 24-well plate.
Add 5 heparin-PEG coated islets or noncoated control islets into each well.
Add serum-supplemented DMEM media into each well to a total volume of 500 µL per well.
Observe tube formation after 4 h and 24 h incubation under a light microscope.
Handpick 30 heparin-PEG coated islets or noncoated control islets into one 1.5 mL tube.
Add 1 mL of physiological salt solution supplemented with 2 mmol/L glucose and incubate at 37 °C for 2 h.
Remove as much solution as possible from each tube.
Stimulate islets by adding 600 µL of physiological salt solution supplemented with 20 mmol/L glucose at 37 °C for 30 min.
Collect 200 μL of supernatant from each tube for insulin ELISA quantification.
